question: Should this PR fail closed on unsafe byte-size config values even when an existing `openclaw.json` contains a formerly accepted unsafe threshold?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and correct, but repository policy treats stricter config validation as compatibility-sensitive because existing setups can stop during config validation.

options.title: Accept Strict Rejection
options.body: Treat unsafe byte thresholds as malformed config and land the PR after rebase and exact-head checks.

options.title: Add Doctor/Warning Path
options.body: Require a pre-merge diagnostic or doctor repair/warning path for unsafe byte-size thresholds before tightening validation.

options.title: Keep Runtime Permissive
options.body: Preserve the old rounding behavior and close or rewrite the PR if maintainers decide compatibility is more important than rejecting unsafe values.

recommendation.title: Accept Strict Rejection
recommendation.body: Treat unsafe byte thresholds as malformed config and land the PR after rebase and exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared byte-size config helper and are currently assigned to the PR.
